findings.finding: Credits Picard replacing dioptric sight openings with telescopes, enabling observations of fixed stars and some planets on the meridian and more accurate distance/altitude measurement. Describes application and advantages; does not expressly identify first inventor or name Gascoigne in this passage.

Selected opening Latin passage agrees in substance with Derham quoted Picard application language. Derham supplies bracketed Royal Academy expansion and truncates continuation with etc.; spelling/capitalization/typographic differences not promoted to changes of technical meaning. Derham himself acknowledges no express inventor designation and infers implication.

Surrounding text discusses older instruments, Huygens pendulum clocks and observational/instrumental arrangements. Technical reports are author claims, not independently authenticated construction or performance. Selected absence of Gascoigne is not an exhaustive volume search or evidence of author access or intent.

Describes stellar measurements, refraction correction and comparisons with Picard observations. Discusses older/modern models and credits Kepler/Cassini; claims solar-table derivation through observations. These are author accounts, not reproduced calibration or raw observation data.

Admits insufficient observations for some lunar terms; discusses Tycho and Le Febvre antecedents. Reports comparing calculations with Observatory lunar eclipses and other observations and deriving a different lunar correction. Fit and reference observations are dependent.

Describes further correction, lunar inclination, unresolved effects and possible atmospheric alternatives. Numerical constants and explanations are published author choices, not authenticated modern uncertainty estimates.

Reports agreement of eclipse calculations from these tables with Observatory observations, after earlier calibration description. Reports discrepancies of many minutes with some other observations and attributes them to instrument defects; that causal judgment is not independently validated here. Promises later planetary tables and fuller star catalog.

Complete inspected preface does not yield an explicit Picard first-inventor designation in the target passage; other named contributors and unresolved technical problems remain visible. Gascoigne was not located in this preface reading; no full-volume absence or author-access/intent claim.
Following numbered page opens angle/time conversion tables, establishing end of preface. Table values not transcribed or validated.
